title: Governor of New Hampshire

context.text: Incumbent Republican Gov. Kelly Ayotte is running for a second two-year term; New Hampshire governors serve two-year terms.
Republican primary (Sept. 8, 2026): Ayotte won renomination with 91.9% of the vote (100,920 votes), ahead of Shaun Fife (4.0%) and Bob Wayne McClory (3.5%).
Democratic primary (Sept. 8, 2026): former Executive Councilor Cinde Warmington won with 96.4% of the vote (126,223 votes), with write-ins receiving the rest.

Stephen Villee, the 2024 Libertarian nominee, is also on the general-election ballot as a Libertarian; Jon Kiper, who switched from the Democratic primary to an independent campaign, is not on the ballot.

candidates.name: Kelly Ayotte
candidates.ballotNote: Won the Sept. 8 Republican primary with 91.9%.

summary.text: Kelly Ayotte is the incumbent Republican governor, first elected in 2024. A former New Hampshire attorney general (2004–2009) and U.S. senator (2011–2017), she has signed legislation rolling back parts of the state's 2018 bail reform law, banning municipal sanctuary policies, and removing the income cap on Education Freedom Accounts, and signed a budget without new taxes but with fee increases.

background.text: Born in Nashua; graduated from Penn State and Villanova University School of Law; worked as a law clerk, prosecutor and deputy attorney general.
Served as New Hampshire's 27th attorney general, 2004–2009, the first woman in that role, then as U.S. senator, 2011–2017; elected governor in 2024.

priorities.text: Public safety and law enforcement: described by NHPR as her calling card, including bail restrictions, outlawing municipal sanctuary policies, and restoring pension benefits for public-safety workers.
No new taxes in the state budget, school choice expansion and state-agency savings targets, according to NHPR's review of her first year.

positions.summary: Signed bills banning municipal sanctuary policies (House Bill 511 and Senate Bill 62, May 22, 2025), and backed a New Hampshire State Police agreement with ICE for troopers to join federal enforcement actions.
positions.quote: There will be no sanctuary cities in New Hampshire. Period. End of story.

positions.summary: Said she would veto any budget that did not earmark funds to boost pensions for public-safety workers who lost benefits.

record.text: Signed House Bill 592, rolling back portions of the state's 2018 bail reform law.

Signed House Bill 511 and Senate Bill 62, anti-sanctuary-city bills that require municipalities to comply with ICE detainers "if safe to do so" and bar local policies restricting cooperation with federal immigration authorities.
Signed Senate Bill 295, which removed the income cap on Education Freedom Accounts (with a 10,000-student cap on enrollment in the program's first year), and a parental bill of rights.

Signed House Bills 1 and 2, a $15.9 billion two-year state budget with no new taxes but many fee increases that also added cost-sharing for people insured through Medicaid and required state agency heads to find unspecified savings.

candidates.researchNotes: Signing dates come from news coverage (Valley News, New Hampshire Bulletin) because the governor's office website and the General Court bill pages blocked automated access. NHPR describes the Medicaid change as copays and the New Hampshire Bulletin as a premium; the item says 'cost-sharing'.

candidates.name: Cinde Warmington
candidates.ballotNote: Won the Sept. 8 Democratic primary with 96.4%.
candidates.currentRole: Former member, New Hampshire Executive Council (2021–2025)

summary.text: Cinde Warmington is the Democratic nominee for governor. A health care attorney, she served on the New Hampshire Executive Council from 2021 to 2025 and lost the 2024 Democratic gubernatorial primary to Joyce Craig. Her platform calls for reversing the Education Freedom Account voucher program, legalizing cannabis, a pledge to veto any income or sales tax, and suspending the gas tax.

background.text: Earned a B.S. from UMass Dartmouth, an MBA from the University of Texas at Arlington and a J.D. from the University of New Hampshire School of Law; practiced health care law for about 20 years.
Served on the Executive Council from 2021 to 2025; lost the 2024 Democratic primary for governor to Joyce Craig.

priorities.text: Affordability: a pledge to veto any income or sales tax, a temporary suspension of the state gas tax, and a 'Cut the Costs' tour focused on property taxes, housing and groceries.
Reverse the Education Freedom Account school voucher program.
priorities.quote: As governor, she will reverse Kelly Ayotte's school voucher scheme, which is driving up property taxes and diverting millions of dollars from public schools

priorities.text: Legalize cannabis; tackle the housing crisis (including appointing a housing czar on day one).

positions.summary: Pledges to reverse New Hampshire's Education Freedom Account voucher program.
positions.quote: As governor, she will reverse Kelly Ayotte's school voucher scheme, which is driving up property taxes and diverting millions of dollars from public schools

positions.summary: Said she has called for no ICE detention facility (a 'human warehouse') anywhere in New Hampshire, including in Merrimack.
positions.quote: NO ICE human warehouse anywhere in New Hampshire.

record.text: Won re-election to the Executive Council in November 2022 with about 60% of the vote, defeating Republican Harold French; she was the council's only Democrat in the 4–1 partisan split that followed.

candidates.researchNotes: Individual Executive Council roll-call votes were not retrieved; the council's own minutes were not reachable in this pass.

candidates.name: Stephen Villee

summary.text: Stephen Villee, a software developer, is a Libertarian candidate for governor and was the party's nominee in 2024.

candidates.researchNotes: Wikipedia, The Green Papers and the New Hampshire Bulletin voter guide list him as the Libertarian candidate; Citizens Count labels him 'Independent/Other' and says he qualified by collecting signatures (the nomination-paper route for candidates outside the two major parties). The NH Secretary of State site blocked automated access, so the printed ballot label could not be checked. No campaign site or coverage found.

researchNotes: New Hampshire has no running mates or lieutenant governor. Ballotpedia was blocked from this environment (bot challenge) and the NH Secretary of State site returned 403. The slate was confirmed against an official sample ballot for the Nov. 3 general election (Dover Ward 1, printed by the Secretary of State), which lists Ayotte (R), Warmington (D) and Villee (Libertarian) for governor. The three-candidate slate (Ayotte, Warmington, Villee) is confirmed by Wikipedia, Citizens Count, The Green Papers and the New Hampshire Bulletin voter guide; Villee's label is Libertarian in three of those and 'Independent/Other' at Citizens Count. Ayotte's record items cite news coverage for signing dates because the governor's office site and General Court bill pages blocked automated access. Ayotte has not published, in the sources found, her own priority statements; her priorities here come from NHPR's year-one review. Warmington's website text includes critical language about Ayotte, which is reported only where it states her own proposals.
